meta.description: GPU reference for the NIM Profile Advisor. pci_device_ids are what NIM matches (gpu_device = <id>:10de). internal_names are NIM manifest 'gpu' tags that are not plain aliases and were mapped from device-id co-occurrence evidence (see gpu_device_validation.json).

gpus.name: NVIDIA L20
gpus.notes: INFERRED: compute capability 8.9 and FP8 support, because L20 is not on the CUDA GPUs page; it uses the AD102 die. 26b7 appears only in pci-ids (not in README), and NIM profiles use 26ba. The K8s label is derived.

gpus.name: NVIDIA L40
gpus.nvlink: Not stated on NVIDIA L40 page (PCIe card)
gpus.notes: Many older LLM NIM manifests label 26b5 as 'L40S' (see the L40S row). By README and pci.ids, 26b5 is the L40. The K8s label is derived.

gpus.name: NVIDIA L40S
gpus.notes: MANIFEST DATA ERROR: older NIM manifests tag 'gpu: L40S' with 'gpu_device: 26b5:10de' (the L40 id). Examples: llama-2-7b-chat_1.0.3:8-9, llama-2-70b-chat_1.0.3:7-8, codellama-13b-instruct_1.2.2:296-297, codellama-34b-instruct_latest:167-168, llama-3-sqlcoder-8b_latest:7-8, llama-3.1-8b-base_1.1.2:312-313, llama-3-taiwan-70b-instruct_latest:342-343, llama-3-swallow-70b-instruct-v0.1_latest:202-203, llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct_1.1.1:692-693, llama-3.2-90b-vision-instruct_1.1.1:580-581. On a real L40S (26b9) those profiles do not match by gpu_device. PCAI: legacy G1 configurations (4, 8 or 16x L40S per search extracts of HPE QuickSpecs; removed from the current v9 QuickSpecs).
sources: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/l40s/ (48GB GDDR6 ECC, 864GB/s, FP8 733/1,466 TFLOPS, 350W, NVLink No, MIG No)

gpus.name: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
gpus.nvlink: NVLink 3, 600 GB/s (A100 datasheet, read via search extract)
gpus.notes: Memory type: the NVIDIA datasheet says HBM2 and the Cosmos NIM table says HBM2e. 20b0 is shared with the A100-PG509-200 board (subsystem 10DE:1450), which gpu_device cannot distinguish. | The device id and subsystem are VERIFIED (README). VRAM, form factor and NVLink are INFERRED because the board shares device 20b0 with the A100 SXM4 40GB; no NVIDIA datasheet for PG509-200 was found. NIM gpu_device '20b0:10de' matches it the same as an A100-SXM4-40GB. The K8s label is derived.

sources: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/a100/ (A100 80GB SXM: 80GB HBM2e, 2,039 GB/s, NVLink 600 GB/s, no FP8 row)

gpus.name: NVIDIA B200
gpus.notes: VALIDATED seed id 2901:10de = NVIDIA B200. VRAM is 180 GB usable (HGX 1.4TB / 8 GPUs; NIM LLM matrix) vs 192 GB nominal (Cosmos). 2909 is a newer B200 id ('HGX B200 168GB' in pci-ids; the 168GB size is unverified). No local manifest uses 2909, so a 2909 host will not match 2901 profiles by gpu_device. 290a 'B200' appears only in pci-ids.
sources: https://pci-ids.ucw.cz/read/PC/10de/2909 (named 'B200' via driver 595.58.03 on 2026-03-24, renamed 'HGX B200 168GB' on 2026-05-08)
https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/hgx/ (HGX B200: 8x Blackwell SXM, 1.4 TB total, NVLink 5 1.8 TB/s, FP4/FP8)

gpus.name: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor
gpus.form_factor: Embedded SoC module (Jetson T5000/T4000; IGX T7000/T5000 boards), unified LPDDR5X
gpus.notes: The device id comes only from community sources (pci-ids and a GitHub issue). Thor is absent from the x86_64 README 595.80. INFERRED: the IGX Thor iGPU uses the same 2b00 id, and T4000 may use a different id. pci-ids also lists 3400 'GB10B [Tegra RP iGPU]' (product unknown). FP8 is INFERRED from CC 11.0 >= 8.9; the NVIDIA page lists only FP4. CUDA 12.9 and older report Thor as sm_101 (10.1), so manifests could carry 10.1. On IGX Thor, NIM would usually match the dGPU (2bb4 or 2bb3). No local manifest references Thor. The K8s label is derived (low confidence).
sources: https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/issues/33296 (2026-10-12, AGX Thor Dev Kit: DRM uevent PCI_ID=10DE:2B00, PCI_SLOT_NAME=0000:01:00.0, DRIVER=nvidia)

https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.0.0/cuda-toolkit-release-notes/index.html (SM101 renumbered to SM110 from CUDA 13.0; search extract)
https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/edge-computing/products/igx/ (IGX Thor: same 2560-core iGPU + dGPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q on Dev Kit/T7000, or RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell on T5000)
https://docs.nvidia.com/igx/user-guide/latest/OV/thor/system-overview-t7000.html (populated dGPU: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition)
